claims.text: Enhanced interface coherency between layers impedes dislocation motion in HEA multilayer coatings.
Impeded dislocation motion reduces time-dependent plastic deformation and creep.
Standard magnetron-sputtering conditions produce relatively incoherent interfaces in the proposed multilayer coating.
Changing magnetron-sputtering deposition parameters can produce higher interface coherency.
Coatings of equal overall thickness can be compared using constant-load nanoindentation creep tests at room and elevated temperatures.
The degree of interface coherency can be characterized by high-resolution TEM or in situ electron microscopy.
More coherent interfaces are strong barriers to dislocation nucleation.
More coherent interfaces are strong barriers to dislocation transmission across layers.
Creep in the proposed coatings is governed substantially by dislocation activity under sustained load.
Restricting the accumulation and movement of dislocations delays the onset of creep deformation.
Coatings with highly coherent interfaces will have lower creep rates and less time-dependent plastic deformation than less coherent baseline coatings.
The proposed behavior applies to magnetron-sputtered HEA multilayer coatings of comparable composition and thickness.
The effect may not extend to bulk HEAs or non-layered coatings because interfaces are less dominant in those materials.
The magnitude of creep-rate reduction is not known precisely.
The creep response may vary with alloy system, applied load, and temperature.
Enhanced-coherency coatings should show both lower creep displacement and reduced dislocation activity relative to the control.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction in creep deformation relative to the control would falsify the hypothesis.
